identity.title: Formation and Atmosphere of Complex Organic Molecules of the HH 212 Protostellar Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have spatially resolved this envelope-disk system with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array at up to $\sim$ 16 AU ($0^{\prime\prime}_{^\textrm{.}}04$) resolution.

evidence.quote: It is deeply embedded in a compact molecular cloud core in the L1630 cloud of Orion, which is at a distance of about 400 pc (cite: Kounkel2017).
It is deeply embedded in a compact molecular cloud core in the L1630 cloud of Orion, which is at a distance of about 400 pc (cite: Kounkel2017).

question.value: Where does a Keplerian disk form inside the infalling-rotating envelope of HH 212, and do the complex organic molecules trace the disk atmosphere (formed in the disk) or a rapidly infalling warm inner envelope?

evidence.quote: Without detailed kinematic study of the envelope and disk, we can not determine the radius at which the Keplerian disk has formed.
Our spatially resolved observations of COMs favor their formation in the disk rather than a rapidly infalling (warm) inner envelope.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00122.S and 2015.1.00024.S.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00122.S and 2015.1.00024.S.
Observations of the HH 212 protostellar system were carried out with ALMA in Band 7 at $\sim$ 350 GHz in Cycles 1 and 3, with 32-45 antennas

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Cycle 1: 4 spws (CO, SiO, HCO+, continuum at 358 GHz); Cycle 3: 6 spws adding SO and H13CO+; 0.212 km/s per channel in line windows

one for HCO$^+$ $J=4-3$ at 356.734288 GHz
CH$_2$DOH (deuterated methanol, 18 lines at 13 frequencies)

sensitivity.value: HCO+: 3.1 mJy/beam (0.06'') and 3.9 mJy/beam (0.1''); COMs: 1.7 mJy/beam (0.848 km/s), 3.0 mJy/beam (0.212 km/s)

evidence.quote: The noise levels are found to be $\sim$ 1.7 mJy beam$^{-1}$ (or $\sim$ 11 K) for 0.848 km s$^{-1}$ and 3.0 mJy beam$^{-1}$ (or $\sim$ 20 K) for 0.212 km s$^{-1}$.
The total time on the HH 212 system is $\sim$ 148 minutes.

analysis_steps.goal: Characterize HCO+ envelope morphology and PV diagrams

method.value: Channel maps at low/high velocity, parabolic boundaries by eye, PV cuts along major and minor axes

evidence.quote: Using a rough eye fitting to the redshifted and blueshifted HCO$^+$ emission of the envelope at both low velocity

key_parameters.value: upper boundary a=0.05, b=0.45; lower a=-0.05, b=-0.6

evidence.quote: we obtained $a=0.05$ and $b=0.45$ for the upper boundary and $a=-0.05$ and $b=-0.6$ for the lower boundary

evidence.quote: rotate our maps by 23$^\circ$ clockwise to align the jet axis in the north-south direction

analysis_steps.goal: Map COM emission and PV structure in the disk atmosphere

method.value: Stack lines of the same molecule for integrated-intensity maps; PV cuts parallel and perpendicular to the disk plane

evidence.quote: Since the emission morphology is similar, the maps of the same molecule are stacked together to make a map with a higher S/N ratio.

fitting.value: Single linear fit to the linear PV structures in methanol and deuterated methanol

evidence.quote: which are obtained from a single linear fit to the linear PV structures seen in both methanol and deuterated methanol

method.value: Toy model with conserved specific angular momentum and energy; model PV outer boundaries matched to observed PV; Keplerian inside centrifugal barrier

evidence.quote: the observed kinematics of the envelope and disk atmosphere can be fitted simultaneously with only two parameters, $l$ and $M$.

key_parameters.value: l and M free; r_c = l^2/GM; r_0 = l^2/2GM

evidence.quote: $$\begin{equation} r_0=\frac{l^2}{2GM} \label{eq:CB} \end{equation}$$

assumptions.value: Flared envelope with parabolic boundaries; fit weighted to blueshifted side because of redshifted self-absorption

evidence.quote: For the envelope, the fit is based more on the blueshifted side, because the redshifted side suffers from self-absorption.

fitting.value: Visual matching of model PV boundaries to observed PV structures; no sampler or likelihood

evidence.quote: These model PV structures can then be used to fit the outer boundaries of the observed PV structures.

validation.value: Model broadly reproduces important PV features of envelope and disk

evidence.quote: In summary, this simple toy model can broadly reproduce all the important features in the PV diagrams of the envelope and disk.

findings_qualitative.value: HCO+ traces an infalling-rotating envelope down to the centrifugal barrier; COMs trace the atmosphere of a Keplerian disk inside it

evidence.quote: This indicates that HCO$^+$ traces the infalling-rotating envelope down to centrifugal barrier and COMs trace the atmosphere of a Keplerian rotating disk within the centrifugal barrier.

findings_qualitative.value: Infall velocity in the COM atmosphere has dropped to zero

evidence.quote: It it clear from the PV diagrams that the infall velocity there has dropped to zero.

claims.hypothesis: Is the ~60 AU dusty disk radius the radius of the centrifugal barrier/Keplerian disk?
claims.experiment: Fit toy infall-rotation model to HCO+ and COM PV diagrams
claims.finding: A Keplerian disk forms inside the centrifugal barrier at ~44 AU

evidence.quote: This indicates that HCO$^+$ traces the infalling-rotating envelope extending down to $\sim$ 44 AU and COMs trace the atmosphere of a Keplerian rotating disk with a radius of $\sim$ 44 AU.

claims.hypothesis: Do COMs trace the disk atmosphere rather than a disk wind or infalling envelope?
claims.experiment: Spatially resolved maps and PV diagrams of CH3OH, CH2DOH, CH3SH, NH2CHO, D2CO
claims.result: Emission 20 AU above and below the midplane, Keplerian rotation, negligible radial velocity
claims.finding: COMs trace the atmosphere of a flared Keplerian disk

evidence.quote: We favor the former interpretation over the latter because, as we will show below, the radial component of the velocity for these layers is much smaller than the rotational component.

claims.hypothesis: Are COMs formed in the disk or in the warm inner envelope?
claims.experiment: Compare COM spatial distribution, Tex and deuteration with models
claims.finding: COMs likely form on grains in the disk and desorb via warming/shock

evidence.quote: all of our detected COMs could be formed in the ice mantle on the dust grains, either in the envelope or in the disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Tex is poorly constrained because data points are scattered at low S/N; may be underestimated by factor ~2

evidence.loc: 3.4 Physical condition in the disk atmosphere

limitations_admitted.value: Disk is optically thick in dust so molecules near the midplane cannot be probed

evidence.quote: Whether such molecules exist closer to the disk midplane cannot be determined for the nearly edge-on disk of HH 212 that is optically thick in dust continuum.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fit is by eye with no formal chi-square or posterior, so uncertainties are loosely defined
Population-diagram result depends on LTE and optically thin assumptions and a shared Tex across species

Conclusions list the mass as 0.25±0.5, inconsistent with ±0.05 in the text
